scope_groups.header: Metal Roofing - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Includes Berridge Cee-Lock standing seam metal roof panel system as indicated on the drawings.
Supply and install high-temp underlayment and self-adhered membrane beneath the roof panel system per keynote 6-06/A4-10.
Supply and install all gutters and downspouts, complete with splash blocks, as indicated.
Accept the roof deck furnished by others as ready to receive the roofing system.
Supply and install all furring, backing, straps, nailers and accessories necessary to support the roofing, fascia and soffit systems.
Coordinate with Framing Subcontractor for eave sheathing (5/8" Dens Glass per Clarification #01 RFI #25) to receive the roofing system.

scope_groups.header: Metal Fascia & Soffit Panels - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Supply and install prefinished metal fascia and soffit panels as indicated, complete with trim, closures and attachment system.
Coordinate edge condition and flashing attachment between the fascia, soffit and roofing systems to maintain manufacturer warranties.
Provide protection of adjacent roofing surfaces during fascia and soffit panel installation.

scope_groups.header: Concessions Pass-Through Counter - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Fabricate and install stainless steel pass-through counter with window header and jambs at the Concessions building per detail 3/A7-10.
Coordinate the rough opening with Framing Subcontractor and the overhead coiling door with Special Doors Subcontractor.
Provide all tests and certifications required for complete and operational systems.
Provide a Manufacturer's Representative for multiple site visits during construction as required to maintain system warranties.
Perform water testing on completed roofing, fascia and soffit systems, and repair deficiencies as required.
Provide temporary roof closures and water stops at the end of each work day to prevent water intrusion.

_open_pm_items: GMP-01, carried from the package record, now RESOLVED by PM ruling 08.06.26 (B1): the GMP governs over Clarification No. 1 RFI #23, and the roof panel system is Berridge Cee-Lock - consistent with A4-20's own roof details (which show Berridge Tee-Panel, Cee-Lock, fascia and wall panel details even in the base bid) and with Foursquare's own scope-review assumption of a 'berrage z lock standing seam roof.' Still flagged because Clarification No. 1 - a document issued to every bidder - states in writing that 'Metal roofing specifications take precedence' over the drawn Berridge callout, the opposite conclusion. No further action needed to draft this exhibit, but the conflict between two contract documents should stay on record in case it resurfaces at shop drawing review.

Contract amount: the awarded_sub record in 01-index/packages/RFP-045.json states Foursquare's price as $135,698 (roofing only). The GMP R2 line 45 and the Procore budget phase code 07-4100-10000 both carry $142,585, the exact sum of Foursquare's two 05.05.26 proposal lines (roofing $135,698 + stainless steel pass-through counter $6,887). This exhibit is drafted to the carried $142,585 and carries the pass-through counter as its own scope group; the package record should be corrected to match.

Sole bidder, late and unsigned: Foursquare is the only bidder CORE carried an award on. Their only proposal on file is flagged 'LATE - not submitted to BuildingConnected' and carries no signed Subcontractor Proposal (Bid) Form. This is a 1% list package under NRS 338.16995 - confirm a properly submitted proposal or Bid Form exists before relying on this record.
Stale pricing: Foursquare's 05.05.26 proposal states a 30-day validity, which expired 06.04.26. No subcontract has issued as of this index date (08.11.26). Confirm current pricing before issuing.

Entity name: Foursquare's own proposal letterhead reads 'Foursquare Roofs & Walls Inc.'; the GMP's 1% Subcontractor Listing (05.27.26) reads 'Foursquare Roof and Walls'. Confirm the correct legal entity name before issuing the subcontract.

Contact info: no email is on file for LaMar Noorda, who signed the base proposal and is named on the scope-review agenda as Foursquare's Project Manager. The only Foursquare email captured in the project record belongs to Gerrit Noorda (Gerrit@foursquarenv.com), used here as the best available contact. Confirm the correct contact before issuing.

Bond rate: no bond rate is on file for Foursquare. The only other bidder, Canyon State, is recorded at 0% on the leveling tab, which the leveling notes themselves flag as a likely BuildingConnected parse artifact rather than a true bond-free quote. Confirm Foursquare's actual bond rate before issuing.

Cross-package pricing flag: Foursquare's 05.19.26 homework response also priced exterior building letters ($6,780 flat metal or $12,892 channel letters) and the outdoor bulletin cabinet ($1,480) at keynotes 6-04 and 6-01/A5-10 - the same figures already open on ITB-072 Building Signage (carried to YESCO). Neither figure is inside the $142,585 carried for RFP-045, confirmed by the amount reconciliation above, so this exhibit excludes that work without routing it. Flagged so the same dollar figures are not read into two packages.

FM Global: the Scope of Work narrative requires 'compliance with requirements of FM Global,' but no other document on this package references an FM Global rating for any material or assembly. Confirm whether FM Global compliance actually applies before relying on it; kept in the review appendix rather than the exhibit pending that confirmation.

intro: Rule 14 keeps out of this exhibit anything the Contract Documents already state, so the Subcontract carries one copy of each obligation rather than two that can drift.

Every line below was drafted, verified and then removed on that basis. All of them still bind the Subcontractor through the document named beneath them. Tick any that should be restated in the Scope of Work above.

items.item: Fabricate and install all counter flashing, cleats, reglets, starter strips, deck sheathing and cover board for the standing seam roof system.
Comply with SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual requirements and standard details for all sheet metal roofing and flashing work.
Provide product data, color samples, and shop drawings indicating material profile, jointing pattern and fastening methods.
Provide manufacturer warranty in accordance with Section 01 7800 Closeout Submittals.
Fabricate gutters and downspouts to SMACNA rectangular profile with brackets, splash pads and downspout extenders.
Install continuous water-resistive barrier lapped to shed water, with head and jamb flashing at all openings and penetrations.
Seal all joints within sheet metal fabrications and at penetrations watertight.
Back paint concealed metal surfaces and surfaces in contact with dissimilar metals.

groups.header: B.  Stated ONLY in a Scope of Work narrative
note: These are the ones worth a decision. If the Scope of Work narrative is not an exhibit to the executed Subcontract, striking these removes the obligation outright rather than relocating it.

items.item: Provide a qualified representative onsite for all tests and inspections, and schedule testing and walk with inspectors to obtain final sign-off.
Comply with the requirements of the Geotechnical Report and Contract Documents for seismic requirements; the most stringent requirement shall prevail.
All materials to comply with flame spread ratings as required, with manufacturer's certifications.
Provide protection along the access path to the roof work area during construction.
Subcontractor is responsible for all receiving, offloading and hoisting of materials for this Scope of Work.
Comply with warranty requirements including coordination and compliance with FM Global.
